report.summary: Reviewed chunk 7 of 13 of containment.py. Contains _nt_open_append and LowIntegrityLog.__init__ and verify. Claims about NtCreateFile vs CreateFileW, share modes, and handle verification are present.
risks: _nt_open_append | medium | Uses hardcoded LOW_APPEND_ACCESS and share mode; if these constants are misdefined, containment may fail. | Verify LOW_APPEND_ACCESS and _FILE_SHARE_READ definitions match expectations.

LowIntegrityLog.__init__ | medium | Opens a second handle with CreateFileW for verification; failure path closes the first handle but may leak if exceptions occur after handle assignment. | Ensure all exception paths close both handles.

LowIntegrityLog.verify | medium | Calls _granted_access and _file_identity which are not defined in this chunk; if those functions are incorrect, verification may be flawed. | Review the implementation of _granted_access and _file_identity.

handoff.purpose: Define _nt_open_append and LowIntegrityLog class with verification logic.

symbols.name: _nt_open_append
symbols.note: Opens a file with NtCreateFile using LOW_APPEND_ACCESS and FILE_SHARE_READ only.

symbols.name: LowIntegrityLog
symbols.note: Manages two handles to a log file, verifying identity and rights before spawn.

symbols.name: LowIntegrityLog.__init__
symbols.note: Opens append handle and verification handle; checks identity and label.

symbols.name: LowIntegrityLog.verify
symbols.note: Re-checks rights and identity of both handles.

claims.text: NtCreateFile grants exactly the requested mask (measured), which is what lets the rights check be an EQUALITY rather than a hopeful subset.
claims.why: The claim about NtCreateFile behavior is based on measurement not present in this chunk; the code uses NtCreateFile but does not provide evidence.

claims.text: CreateFileW asked for 0x00100004 and produced a handle with GrantedAccess 0x00100084 -- it adds rights of its own accord.
claims.why: This claim refers to CreateFileW behavior not demonstrated in this chunk; code uses CreateFileW only for verification handle but does not compare masks.

claims.text: The share mode is FILE_SHARE_READ ONLY. Not sharing DELETE is load-bearing and was found by measurement: with FILE_SHARE_DELETE the contained child deleted its own log by path (the file is Low, so a Low process may delete it) and could then have written a replacement full of fabricated gate output.
claims.why: The code sets share mode to _FILE_SHARE_READ only (line 739). The claim about DELETE sharing is not contradicted by this chunk.

claims.text: Not sharing WRITE stops the same trick via truncate-and-rewrite.
claims.why: The code does not include FILE_SHARE_WRITE in share mode, so write sharing is not granted.

claims.text: The single handle allowed across the containment boundary.
claims.why: The claim that only this class's handle crosses the boundary is not verifiable within this chunk; it depends on spawn_contained usage not present.

claims.text: A caller cannot hand spawn_contained a raw handle: the parameter is typed to this class and nothing else is accepted.
claims.why: The spawn_contained function signature is not in this chunk; we cannot verify the type enforcement.

claims.text: TWO handles are held, and only one of them is inheritable: handle (APPEND|SYNCHRONIZE, inheritable) and _verify (READ_CONTROL, NOT inheritable).
claims.why: In __init__, _handle is opened with _OBJ_INHERIT (line 733), while _verify is opened via CreateFileW (no inherit flag) and is not added to any inheritance list.

claims.text: Reading the mandatory label needs READ_CONTROL, and granting the child READ_CONTROL is not on the table, so the label is read through a second handle whose FILE IDENTITY is proven equal to the first.
claims.why: In __init__, _verify is opened with _READ_CONTROL (line 754) and identity is compared (line 762). The claim that child does not get READ_CONTROL is not contradicted.

claims.text: Both stay open for the lifetime of the object, so the file object cannot be swapped underneath the check.
claims.why: The lifetime management (close method) is not fully shown; we see close() is called on exception but the rest of the class is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Re-check target and rights ON THE HANDLES. Raises, never returns bad.
claims.why: verify() raises ContainmentUnavailable on any failure; no return value is used.

claims.text: Called again from spawn_contained because construction and spawn are not the same instant, and a check that is not re-run at the moment of use is a time-of-check/time-of-use bug wearing a guard's hat.
claims.why: The call from spawn_contained is not present in this chunk.

observations.what: The function _nt_open_append uses hardcoded constants (LOW_APPEND_ACCESS, _FILE_SHARE_READ) that are not defined in this chunk.
LowIntegrityLog.__init__ opens a second handle with CreateFileW and compares identities; if identity check passes, it assumes both handles refer to same file.
verify() calls _granted_access and _file_identity, which are not defined in this chunk.
The error message in verify() mentions APPEND|READ_ATTRIBUTES|SYNCHRONIZE but the constant LOW_APPEND_ACCESS might not include READ_ATTRIBUTES.
